subject.title: [BUG] exec tool: aborted run wedges subsequent exec calls in same session (regression from PR #94412)

question: Should this issue be treated as covered by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102160 once that integration stack lands, or should maintainers require a separate live exec-abort reproduction before closing it?
rationale: The candidate stack plausibly fixes the shared lifecycle class, but the current issue's exact exec-after-abort wedge has not been proven fixed by that PR or current main.

options.title: Require exact exec proof after integration
options.body: Keep this issue open until the integration stack lands and a focused proof shows a later trivial exec succeeds after the reported abort/stall path.

options.title: Fold into the lifecycle stack now
options.body: Treat this issue as tracked by the broader run-lifecycle PR and close it only when that PR lands with maintainer-accepted soak evidence.

options.title: Queue a separate narrow investigation
options.body: Ask for a standalone exec-abort reproduction if maintainers believe the stack may not cover the process-session slot leak described here.

recommendation.title: Require exact exec proof after integration
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the integration stack lands and a focused proof shows a later trivial exec succeeds after the reported abort/stall path.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the lifecycle umbrella and the integration PR that is the strongest candidate fix for this report's class.
